ABP1.review: Several students describe him as easygoing and say exams require lengthy written answers.
One student says he shares exam suggestions shortly before quizzes and midterms and questions follow them; assessments are manageable, B+ is attainable, and more effort can earn A/A-.
A student reports earning an A- through attentive participation, describes him as friendly, and says he allows makeups and added rather than deducted marks before the final.
Some students say grades are often around B/B+, with A/A- difficult or uncommon even after strong effort; one reports receiving B+ instead of the grade expected.

One reviewer says his lectures are not very engaging, but worksheets before exams, an easy solo presentation and learning-outcome task, and maintaining a positive relationship can make doing well manageable.
A detailed negative review reports no curve, limited marks despite strong work, only one A in the section, and an average grade; the reviewer strongly advises choosing another faculty.

AGR2.review: Students describe him as friendly and fun and say exam questions are direct and easy when studied from the slides.
A student says he values interaction: attend and participate, write on the board, and make sure he knows your name; being a class representative gave that reviewer an advantage.
Students say he gives quiz and exam suggestions and appreciates long, relevant answers; with steady effort, strong grades including A/A- are achievable.

ASZ.review: A detailed reviewer calls him a knowledgeable, humble historian who teaches Bengal's history through storytelling. Quizzes can be tricky, but attendance and notes make exams and viva manageable; grades are described as deserved, an A is possible, and he usually does not curve.

Some students say his lectures are long and require detailed notes; lecture content may not match the slides, missing class makes the course difficult, and it may be hard if ancient or medieval history does not interest you.

MBK1.review: Students repeatedly praise her as very good and easygoing, advising students to attend, take notes, and follow her guidance on what matters for exams.
A student says her teaching is story-based and questions follow what she teaches in class; attend, take notes, and answer in the same narrative style.

MDI1.review: Several students call him one of the best or a goated faculty member.
A student advises attending regularly and participating; he may seem strict about marks, but reportedly curves, and a well-prepared final is important.
A student says his classes often focus on local culture, politics, religion, and songs rather than the slides.

One reviewer says he makes the course unnecessarily complicated and hard to learn from; grades may depend on familiarity and communication, and the reviewer objects to class presentation videos being collected for YouTube.

SLN.review: Several students describe the course as very difficult, report receiving a C or needing a retake, and strongly recommend avoiding her.
A detailed firsthand account describes feeling demeaned, having correct work undervalued, and seeing unfair or preferential grading; the overall class experience was stressful and unpleasant.
Another student says they worked consistently but received a disappointing final grade, felt their effort was not reflected, and strongly advises against taking her.
A student who earned an A- says the workload is substantial but manageable with punctual attendance and thorough notes; they describe her as strict but did not personally observe bias.
A student says regular attendance and detailed notes can make A/A- possible, though substantial effort is required.
One student says she gave marks generously in their experience, including overlooking spelling mistakes.
A student says she teaches history as a story; note everything, ask what can be skipped, and expect questions from both readings and lectures.
A student says she does not curve and makes exam questions hard.

ZRS.review: A detailed review praises her clear, engaging teaching and sweet manner. Quizzes can be somewhat tough but stay within class lectures and slides; the reviewer says she gives good marks and curves.
